raw_response:
I farm 13.1 mu, so I will not spread myself too thin. Since my family has some off-farm work, I will keep the main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way I know to bring in grain, and I can manage it with the well. I will put about 10 mu into wheat-maize and keep 3.1 mu in cotton. That is close to what I would trust around here: wheat and maize pay the basic bills, and cotton gives me some cash if the price is decent. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will stay a little on the safe side, especially for wheat and maize on irrigated land. For wheat, I will use enough nitrogen to hold the tillers and fill grain, with phosphorus under the base fertilizer and some potassium so the straw does not fall flat. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep plant stand neat, push nitrogen a bit because maize eats hard in summer, and use two irrigations if rain is short. For cotton, I will not put too much area because it takes more watching and more sprays, but on a few mu I can still manage it carefully. I will follow what has worked in recent years, only adjusting rates a little for cost and the well water I have.
